title: Two identical green candles can have opposite volume delta. What do you check beyond OHLCV?
author: RobodOfficial
selftext:
Two identical green candles can have opposite volume delta. What do you check beyond OHLCV?

**Disclosure:** We’re the team behind Robod, a crypto research and account analytics platform.

A green candle means the closing price was above the opening price. It doesn’t necessarily mean aggressive buying exceeded aggressive selling.

Every executed trade has both a buyer and a seller. Taker volume distinguishes which side traded aggressively against resting liquidity.

Here’s a **hypothetical example**, using two one-minute perpetual bars:

Both have the same open, high, low and close: **100 / 103 / 99 / 102**. Both trade **1,000 units**.

|Metric|Bar A|Bar B|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Taker buy volume|650|450|
|Taker sell volume|350|550|
|Volume delta|\+300|−100|
|Open interest change|\+2%|−2%|

**The OHLCV candles are identical. The underlying activity isn’t.**

Bar A has net aggressive buying and expanding open interest. Bar B closes higher despite net aggressive selling, while open interest contracts.

Neither combination predicts the next move. Open interest alone also doesn’t identify whether long or short positions drove a price change.

When researching a setup, these are separate questions worth checking:

* **Flow:** Is cumulative volume delta strengthening alongside price, or diverging?
* **Positioning:** Is open interest expanding or contracting?
* **Coverage:** Do all the fields being studied actually cover the same historical period?
* **Quality:** Are there gaps or carried-forward values that could distort the interpretation?

More data can make a hypothesis more specific. Whether it improves a strategy still needs testing with defined entries, exits and costs.

**For traders who use order flow: which additional check has been most useful alongside OHLCV, and how did you evaluate whether it added value?**

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Taker delta plus OI change is the whole game. Bar B closing green on negative delta with OI contracting is just shorts covering, not real demand. Test it with fixed entries and costs before you trust it.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I don't trade order flow myself, so this comes from how I'd test it. Beyond candles, one extra field I'd check on perps is funding, since it shows how crowded one side is. To see if it adds value, I'd run the same simple rule with and without it on data the rule never saw, with fees included, and count how many versions I tried so I'm not just picking the lucky one. Your point about gaps and carried-forward values matters too, because a filled value can look like a signal. Cymetica's Funding Rate Radar shows perp funding across venues, normalized to the same period.

comments.author: Infamous_Food_3766
comments.body: how are u lining up the oi snapshots with the candles? would be useful to show the timestamps for both, especially if oi updates less often than the bars. i'd want to check that before testing whether the extra field helps.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: coverage bites on equities too. the taker side isn't in the consolidated tape for stocks, so you're inferring it with the tick rule or Lee-Ready, and that misclassifies often enough on fast one minute bars that the delta itself becomes an estimate.
